concrete.why: SNG-250 §3 ITEM: 'the effect is a real rules-resolvable thing (heals N / grants function F / opens X), not "hums with old power"'. Grounded in the code, rules-resolvable means EXACTLY one of two things: bonusTags the roll can match (equipmentBonus/wieldBonusFor), or numeric effects.health/energy the spend can apply (consumeItem). An item with neither is inert — it can be carried and described and can never once change a roll or a state.

a consumable with no numeric effects is the sharpest form of the hollow item: consumeItem (inventory.js:224) DESTROYS the stack and returns {} — the player spends a real resource and provably nothing happens. usableCombatItems will not even offer it as a move.

theConcreteLayer: CCODE-55 (SNG-250 §3/§4): each contentType may declare a `concrete` array beside `topLevel`. `topLevel` answers SNG-250's WHOLE question (does every consumer-read field carry a value?); `concrete` answers its CONCRETE question (is that value a real thing the rules can ACT on, or a word?). Every rule is machine-checkable and code-grounded — no rule here encodes a judgement, only a fact the engine already relies on. Rule vocabulary: `enum` (value in the listed set), `everyInVocab` (every array member resolves in a named content vocab), `nonEmptyArray`, `numberInRange`, `someNumeric` (an object has a numeric value at one of `keys`), `anyOf` (at least one nested rule holds), `impliesSomeNumeric` (when `whenField` is truthy, `field` must have a numeric value at one of `keys`). ONE gate reads this for every type — a new type declares its contract here and is gated without new gate code (SNG-250 §5).
lanes: SNG-250 §4 OWNERSHIP. CCode owns the MECHANICAL half of this file — which fields a consumer reads, their types, and the `concrete` rules above, every one traceable to a real read or a real clamp in HEAD. Aevi owns the SEMANTIC half — the per-type vague/concrete PROSE markers ('wants the forge her brother left' vs 'wants respect'), which no static rule can decide. Those markers are deliberately NOT invented here; the §3 semantic bar for npc/item/creature/skill is Aevi's to author, and the gate will read them from this same file when they land (a `vagueMarkers` array per type is the natural slot).
howTheSweepUsesThis: For each contentType, for each authored instance, assert every non-optional field here is PRESENT and (where typed) correctly TYPED. CRASH-severity missing = the build must fail (a consumer throws). EMPTY = fail (renders broken - the visible class). DEGRADED = warn (works but hollow - e.g. no image) unless Erik promotes it. The generator round-trip (§5c) runs its OUTPUT through this same map. Grows by incident: a new consumer.read that breaks on absence adds a line here + the sweep covers it.
provenance: Every field verified at origin by grepping the consumer code for X.subfield reads (2026-07-25): quest reads app.js~6070-6130/7291; npc reads gm.js (25x .name) + SNG-233 directive; location reads random_encounters.js/SNG-180; creature reads random_encounters.js. Non-speculative - if a field isn't read by a real consumer, it's NOT here (no bloat, the SNG-232 lesson).
